raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On a PD decode server, a request within `--num-reserved-decode-tokens` (default 512) of the decode KV pool size passes every intake check and then never fits, even when the pool is empty. There are two ways to get there:

1. **Fresh prompt.** `pop_preallocated` never preallocates it and stops at it, so every request queued behind it waits as well.
2. **Retracted request.** A request that has decoded most of its `max_new_tokens` and then gets retracted never resumes. `pop_preallocated` also subtracts its reservation from every fresh request's budget, so nothing is admitted after it. The decode server stalls until the requests time out or are aborted. This case does not need a long prompt: a 64-token prompt that has generated close to its limit is enough.

The decode server runs the normal intake. `init_req_max_new_tokens` clamps `max_new_tokens` so the prompt plus its output fits the pool, and `validate_input_length` and `_check_if_req_exceed_kv_capacity` accept the request. `_required_admission_tokens` (preallocation) and `_prealloc_required_tokens` (retracted resume, and the retracted reservation charged in `_allocatable_token_budgets`) then add the full `num_reserved_decode_tokens` on top of the request's KV. That is up to 512 tokens more than the request can still decode.

This is reachable whenever the decode pool holds fewer tokens than `context_len`, so that the pool bounds intake. That is common for long-context models on decode nodes with a small KV budget.

## Modifications

- New `DecodePreallocQueue._decode_reserve_tokens(req)` returns `min(num_reserved_decode_tokens, max_new_tokens - len(output_ids) + 1)`, which is the decode slots the request can still use, including the pending token. Both `_required_admission_tokens` and `_prealloc_required_tokens` use it for the request's own reservation, and the SWA side follows the full side as before. The reservations kept for other active requests (`num_reserved_decode_tokens * n_active`) are unchanged.
- New CPU test `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_decode_prealloc_admission.py`, with page sizes 1 and 16. It takes the decode limits from `TpModelWorker.get_worker_info` and the request from `init_req_max_new_tokens` and `validate_input_length`, and uses a real token allocator. The KV receiver, the final `_pre_alloc` copy and `restore_kv_cache` are stubbed, as in the existing prealloc queue tests.
  - `test_longest_accepted_prompt_is_preallocated_on_an_empty_pool`: the longest prompt the intake accepts must be preallocated.
  - `test_retracted_request_near_its_length_limit_resumes_on_an_empty_pool`: a retracted request one token short of its `max_new_tokens` must resume.
  - On `main`, all 4 subtests fail.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable. This only changes a scheduling bound.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Not applicable. There is nothing on the hot path.

Correctness evidence, CPU only. These use real SGLang intake and real `pop_preallocated` / `resume_retracted_reqs` budget logic on an empty real allocator, with no model and no GPU.

Fresh prompt: one request with `max_tokens` unset and a short request queued behind it, for every prompt length in the last 700 tokens of the pool. The table counts prompts that passed intake but were never preallocated:

| page_size | decode KV tokens | main efc9849520 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4096 | 505 (3585–4089) | 0 |
| 16 | 4096 | 505 (3585–4089) | 0 |
| 64 | 8192 | 505 (7681–8185) | 0 |

Retracted request: a 64-token prompt retracted after generating each of the last 700 output lengths it is allowed, with a fresh request queued. The table counts requests that never resumed:

| page_size | decode KV tokens | main efc9849520 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4096 | 508 (3522–4029 output tokens) | 0 |
| 16 | 4096 | 493 (3522–4014) | 0 |
| 64 | 8192 | 445 (7618–8062) | 0 |

On `main`, the request queued behind was not admitted in any of the stuck cases above.

I also ran the new test and the existing CPU tests that drive the prealloc queue (`test_priority_scheduling_disaggregation.py`, `test_decode_radix_lock_ref.py`, `test_decode_retraction_backup.py`, `test_mamba_capacity.py`, `test_prefill_complete_integration.py`, `test_unified_memory_move_gate.py`, `test_decode_queue_cleanup.py`, `test_admission_abort_not_enqueued.py`) on both trees. The only failures specific to `main` are the 4 new subtests, and nothing fails only on this branch. The other failures are the same on both trees. All of them are in `test_decode_retraction_backup.py` and need CUDA, which my machine does not have.

I also ran a scheduler-level check. A CPU driver runs the real `Scheduler` in decode mode with the fake transfer backend and the decode radix cache on, so requests go through `process_decode_queue`, preallocation, the fake transfer, the commit of the synthetic handoff token, and decode. On `main`, all 30 seeds stopped making progress: the prealloc queue held dozens of requests while the pool was completely free, for example `prealloc 57 … free 256` on a 256-token pool. With this change all 30 seeds finished. One caveat: the driver's pools are small (160–512 tokens), so the default 512-token reserve alone exceeds the pool and every request is affected. On a production-sized pool, only requests close to capacity hit it.

I have not run an end-to-end PD deployment.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). I ran isort 7.0.0, ruff 0.15.1 (check and format) and codespell 2.4.1 on the changed files.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not needed.

files.patch:
@@ -566,13 +566,22 @@ def _required_admission_tokens(
         self, req: Req, allocated_tokens: int, prefix_len: int, retractable_tokens: int
     ) -> int:
         return max(
-            allocated_tokens + self.num_reserved_decode_tokens,
+            allocated_tokens + self._decode_reserve_tokens(req),
             pre_alloc_fill_len(req)
             - prefix_len
             + min(req.sampling_params.max_new_tokens, CLIP_MAX_NEW_TOKEN)
             - retractable_tokens,
         )
 
+    def _decode_reserve_tokens(self, req: Req) -> int:
+        # Intake fit the prompt plus max_new_tokens into the pool. Reserving the
+        # full decode headroom past what the request can still decode would not
+        # fit even an empty pool, and the queue stops at the first such request.
+        remaining_decode_slots = (
+            req.sampling_params.max_new_tokens - len(req.output_ids) + 1
+        )
+        return min(self.num_reserved_decode_tokens, max(remaining_decode_slots, 0))
+
     def _prealloc_reservation_fits(
         self,
         full_tokens: int,
@@ -654,11 +663,12 @@ def _prealloc_required_tokens(self, req: Req) -> Tuple[int, int]:
             # Match the allocator, which charges whole pages for both pools.
             full_len = ceil_align(full_len, page_size)
             swa_len = ceil_align(swa_len, page_size)
-        swa_reserved = self.num_reserved_decode_tokens
+        decode_reserved = self._decode_reserve_tokens(req)
+        swa_reserved = decode_reserved
         if get_memory().disable_radix_cache:
             swa_reserved = 0
         return (
-            full_len + self.num_reserved_decode_tokens,
+            full_len + decode_reserved,
             swa_len + swa_reserved,
         )

@@ -0,0 +1,190 @@
+"""Decode-side preallocation must admit every prompt the decode intake accepts.
+
+The decode server clamps max_new_tokens so the prompt plus its output fits the
+KV pool. Preallocation then also reserved num_reserved_decode_tokens on top of
+the prompt, so a prompt within that reserve of the pool size was accepted but
+never preallocated, even on an empty pool, and every request queued behind it
+waited forever.
+"""
+
+import functools
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.disaggregation.decode import DecodePreallocQueue
+from sglang.srt.managers.schedule_batch import Req
+from sglang.srt.managers.scheduler import Scheduler
+from sglang.srt.managers.tp_worker import TpModelWorker
+from sglang.srt.managers.utils import validate_input_length
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.allocator.base import BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.allocator.paged import PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.allocator.token import TokenToKVPoolAllocator
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import publish, reset_context
+from sglang.srt.sampling.sampling_params import SamplingParams
+from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+KV_CAPACITY = 4096
+NUM_RESERVED_DECODE_TOKENS = 512
+
+
+class TestDecodePreallocAdmission(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        reset_context()
+        self.addCleanup(reset_context)
+        publish(ServerArgs(model_path="dummy"), role="tokenizer")
+
+    def _new_allocator(self, page_size):
+        if page_size == 1:
+            return TokenToKVPoolAllocator(
+                KV_CAPACITY, torch.float16, "cpu", None, False
+            )
+        return PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator(
+            KV_CAPACITY, page_size, torch.float16, "cpu", None, False
+        )
+
+    def _decode_intake_limits(self, allocator):
+        worker = SimpleNamespace(
+            model_runner=SimpleNamespace(
+                effective_logical_max_total_num_tokens=KV_CAPACITY,
+                logical_max_total_num_tokens=KV_CAPACITY,
+                token_to_kv_pool_allocator=allocator,
+                max_running_requests=4,
+                forward_stream=None,
+                req_to_token_pool=SimpleNamespace(size=4, max_context_len=1 << 20),
+                token_to_kv_pool=SimpleNamespace(size=KV_CAPACITY),
+            ),
+            # A context longer than the decode pool, so the pool bounds intake.
+            model_config=SimpleNamespace(context_len=1 << 20),
+            dllm_algorithm=None,
+            random_seed=0,
+            device="cpu",
+        )
+        info = TpModelWorker.get_worker_info(worker)
+        return info[4], info[5]
+
+    def _accepted_req(self, rid, prompt_len, scheduler, max_req_input_len):
+        req = Req(rid, "", [7] * prompt_len, SamplingParams(max_new_tokens=None))
+        req.sampling_params.normalize(None)
+        req.output_ids = [8]  # the first token, sampled by the prefill server
+        Scheduler.init_req_max_new_tokens(scheduler, req)
+        self.assertIsNone(validate_input_length(req, max_req_input_len, False))
+        self.assertFalse(req.finished())
+        return req
+
+    def _new_queue(self, allocator, reqs):
+        queue = DecodePreallocQueue.__new__(DecodePreallocQueue)
+        queue.pp_size = 1
+        queue.queue = [
+            SimpleNamespace(
+                req=req,
+                waiting_for_input=True,
+                kv_receiver=MagicMock(),
+                metadata_buffer_index=-1,
+                is_rebootstrap=False,
+                host_staged=False,
+            )
+            for req in reqs
+        ]
+        queue.pending_reqs = []
+        queue.retracted_queue = []
+        queue.num_reserved_decode_tokens = NUM_RESERVED_DECODE_TOKENS
+        queue.max_total_num_tokens = KV_CAPACITY
+        queue._num_published_destinations = 0
+        queue._resolve_pending_reqs = MagicMock()
+        queue._update_handshake_waiters = MagicMock()
+        queue._pre_alloc = MagicMock(return_value=torch.arange(4))
+        queue.req_to_token_pool = MagicMock()
+        queue.req_to_token_pool.available_size.return_value = 100
+        queue.req_to_token_pool.mamba_allocator = None
+        queue.req_to_token_pool.holds_state_slots = False
+        queue.req_to_metadata_buffer_idx_allocator = MagicMock()
+        queue.req_to_metadata_buffer_idx_allocator.available_size.return_value = 100
+        queue.req_to_metadata_buffer_idx_allocator.alloc.side_effect = iter(range(100))
+        queue.token_to_kv_pool_allocator = allocator
+        queue.token_to_kv_pool = MagicMock()
+        queue.transfer_queue = SimpleNamespace(queue=[], enable_staging=False)
+        queue.kv_manager = SimpleNamespace(kv_args=SimpleNamespace(state_types=[]))
+        queue.tree_cache = MagicMock()
+        scheduler = MagicMock()
+        scheduler.enable_priority_scheduling = False
+        scheduler.running_batch.reqs = []
+        scheduler.enable_hisparse = False
+        scheduler.enable_lora = False
+        scheduler.enable_decode_hicache = False
+        scheduler.waiting_queue = []
+        scheduler.last_batch = None
+        queue.scheduler = scheduler
+        return queue
+
+    def _intake_scheduler(self, allocator, page_size, max_req_len):
+        allocator.max_new_tokens_for_memory = functools.partial(
+            BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator.max_new_tokens_for_memory, allocator
+        )
+        return SimpleNamespace(
+            max_new_tokens_limit=None,
+            max_req_len=max_req_len,
+            max_total_num_tokens=KV_CAPACITY,
+            kv_shard_widening=1,
+            page_size=page_size,
+            token_to_kv_pool_allocator=allocator,
+            sliding_window_size=None,
+            chunked_prefill_size=None,
+        )
+
+    def test_longest_accepted_prompt_is_preallocated_on_an_empty_pool(self):
+        for page_size in (1, 16):
+            with self.subTest(page_size=page_size):
+                allocator = self._new_allocator(page_size)
+                max_req_len, max_req_input_len = self._decode_intake_limits(allocator)
+                scheduler = self._intake_scheduler(allocator, page_size, max_req_len)
+                # validate_input_length accepts prompts shorter than the limit.
+                longest = self._accepted_req(
+                    "longest", max_req_input_len - 1, scheduler, max_req_input_len
+                )
+                short = self._accepted_req("short", 16, scheduler, max_req_input_len)
+                queue = self._new_queue(allocator, [longest, short])
+                self.assertFalse(queue._check_if_req_exceed_kv_capacity(longest))
+
+                with patch("sglang.srt.disaggregation.decode.CLIP_MAX_NEW_TOKEN", 4096):
+                    preallocated, failed = queue.pop_preallocated()
+
+                # The short request waits for the pool the longest one now holds.
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    [decode_req.req.rid for decode_req in preallocated], ["longest"]
+                )
+                self.assertEqual(failed, [])
+
+    def test_retracted_request_near_its_length_limit_resumes_on_an_empty_pool(self):
+        for page_size in (1, 16):
+            with self.subTest(page_size=page_size):
+                allocator = self._new_allocator(page_size)
+                max_req_len, max_req_input_len = self._decode_intake_limits(allocator)
+                scheduler = self._intake_scheduler(allocator, page_size, max_req_len)
+                retracted = self._accepted_req(
+                    "retracted", 64, scheduler, max_req_input_len
+                )
+                # Retracted one token before its max_new_tokens limit.
+                retracted.output_ids = [8] * (
+                    retracted.sampling_params.max_new_tokens - 1
+                )
+                retracted.is_retracted = True
+                fresh = self._accepted_req("fresh", 16, scheduler, max_req_input_len)
+                queue = self._new_queue(allocator, [fresh])
+                queue.retracted_queue = [retracted]
+
+                with patch("sglang.srt.disaggregation.decode.restore_kv_cache"):
+                    resumed = queue.resume_retracted_reqs()
+
+                self.assertEqual(resumed, [retracted])
+                self.assertEqual(queue.retracted_queue, [])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
